transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-04 14:05 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Redwood Solutions Eng), Maya Ortiz (Redwood Product), Dr. Priya Rao (PioneerHealth CTO), Ethan Brooks (PioneerHealth ML Eng), Lena Park (PioneerHealth Security Ops), Marcus Hill (PioneerHealth VP Product)

Summary (auto): quick model catalog walkthrough showing open model selection, benchmarks, and compatibility matrix. Discussed hosted vs dedicated, quantization tradeoffs, VPC requirements, and security artifacts. Next steps: pricing and benchmarks, sample workload for pilot.

[00:00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this to about 45 minutes, demo the model catalog in the Console, show how to pick open models and run bench marks, and then we'll go over compatibility matrices for Dedicated/Private.
[00:00:10] Dr. Priya Rao: Great, thanks. Quick context: PioneerHealth processes clinician notes and patient messages, low latency is important for triage workflows but cost is also a big concern. We're exploring hosted first and then maybe Dedicated for certain loads.
[00:00:28] Alex: Perfect, that's exactly what we'll focus on. Samira, want to jump into the Console?
[00:00:33] Samira (SE): Yep, sharing screen now. So this is the Redwood Console model catalog. Top-left you can filter by task - generation, chat, embeddings, reranking. For open models we curate a set with verified performance profiles. You can see model family, size, quantization options, and a bench mark column.
[00:00:00] [screen glitch]
[00:01:05] Samira: Sorry little lag. For PioneerHealth I'd highlight the mid-size open models - they hit a good balance for latency and cost. See this compatibility badge - Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (VPC) each have checks. The matrix shows whether a given quantized variant is supported on a GPU type and whether we support KV cache for chat with that variant.
[00:01:30] Ethan: Can you explain the compatibility badge a bit more? We use 2 different GPUs in our lab and sometimes on prem racks.
[00:01:36] Jordan: Sure, the compatibility matrix maps model variant -> supported runtimes -> recommended GPU families. For example, this Llama-derivative 13B quantized to 4-bit has a green check for our A100 and H100 pools under Dedicated, but for some older T4 configs it shows yellow (possible but reduced perf) or red (not recommended). Note: our matrix also flags when custom kernel compilation is required.
[00:02:00] Lena: Do you have to recompile kernels for every quantization? We have strict change control so that matters.
[00:02:07] Samira: Often we pick prebuilt kernels for common quant profiles; for more experimental quantiztions we run a short build step. We surface that in the catalog as a note, "kernel compile may be required." We'll share the matrix and the build time estimates in the benchmark sheet.
[00:02:25] Marcus: Benchmarks - are they synthetic or on customer data?
[00:02:30] Alex: We do both. The catalog shows our canonical benchmarks (synthetic, 150-token prompts) and we attach reproducible scripts. For accurate numbers we recommend you run the included bench script with your sample dataset - that will also highlight token distribution and prefix cache hit rates.
[00:02:50] Samira: Here's an example benchmark row: model name, quant level, tokens/sec, median p50 latency, p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens estimate. Note the cost estimate assumes our default batching and caching config; you can tune those in Redwood Optimize.
[00:03:10] Dr. Priya Rao: Speaking of Optimize, can you show how it recommends batching and quantization for a workload like ours?
[00:03:16] Maya (Product): Sure - switching to Optimize tab. We ingest a small profile of your traffic (or you can upload a sample). Optimize simulates different batching sizes, KV cache TTLs, and quant profiles and surfaces a pareto front of latency vs cost. For triage we typically optimize for 95th percentile latency under 300ms and then minimize cost.
[00:03:36] [00:03:40] Ethan: If we choose a heavy quant profile, how often do you see quality regressions? We care about clinical nuance.
[00:03:46] Samira: Great question. That's where our quality guards come in - we run evals on your prompt sets; the console will show disagreement metrics vs a reference model. We also support A/B rollouts so you can compare outputs before doing a full switch. Some medical entity recognition tasks are sensitive to 4-bit quantization; we flag those and provide recommended fallback profiles.
[00:04:10] Lena: For security: can you describe data flow for hosted inference? Does Redwood retain raw text? We need SOC2 controls and KMS integration.
[00:04:19] Alex: For hosted, by default request logs are retained for 30 days for observability and debugging but can be turned off for enterprise. We have KMS integrations and HSM support for Private deployments. We will send SOC2 docs and network diagrams - there's a doc link in the chat.
[00:04:33] Dr. Priya Rao: What about SSO and RBAC?
[00:04:36] Jordan: SAML/SCIM SSO is supported for the Console, and RBAC can be scoped to teams and models. For Dedicated and Private you can bring your own identity provider with SCIM provisioning.
[00:04:50] Alex: Now back to the catalog - I'll walk through selecting an open model for embeddings+rerank use case. 
[00:04:55] Samira: We generally recommend starting with a smaller embedding model to index notes, and a mid-size chat model for context-aware reranks. In the catalog you can filter by embedding dimension, license (important), and whether model weights are allowed to be run in Private.
[00:05:20] [00:05:30] Samira: Note: some open checkpoints have license NSFW/clauses, we annotate these; legal flagged ones appear with a red clip icon.
[00:05:40] Ethan: Any known issues with de-tokenization or special tokens that break our tokenizers? We use a BPE variant.
[00:05:46] Samira: The compatibility matrix lists tokenizer families and whether we detect differences. If a model uses a different BPE vocab you can upload a mapping and we can run a tokenizer compat check in the bench script.
[00:06:05] Marcus: If we want Dedicated later, how seamless is the move? Do we need to change API calls?
[00:06:11] Alex: One of our differentiators is unified API - same endpoint semantics across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. You may change the endpoint or routing policy, but the client SDKs are identical. Canary rollouts are first-class so you can cut over traffic gradually.
[00:06:30] [00:06:40] Dr. Priya Rao: Latency numbers - what should we realistically expect for a 13B model at 150 tokens with our latency SLOs?
[00:06:46] Samira: On H100 Dedicated with 4-bit quant + KV cache warm, p50 can be sub-80ms and p95 around 180-220ms depending on batching. On Hosted shared pools p95 is higher because of queuing. We'll include model-specific p95s in the sheet.
[00:07:10] Ethan: How does caching interact with multi-tenant hosted pools? If a patient session spans requests, will KV cache help?
[00:07:18] Jordan: KV cache is per-session and in Dedicated we can pin caches to GPU-local memory which gives best hit rates. On Hosted we provide a tuned cache layer that gives good benefits but it's multi-tenant so cold-starts happen more. Optimize suggests prefix caching TTLs based on your traffic patterns.
[00:07:40] [00:07:45] Lena: For compliance we need audit logs of who invoked which model and which model version.
[00:07:49] Alex: Audit logs are included in enterprise plan, with token-level attribution and route-level metadata for every request. Private deployments can ship logs to your SIEM.
[00:08:05] Samira: Back to model selection - here's a concrete selection flow: pick a model family, choose quant level (8-bit, 4-bit), check compatibility matrix, then run bench script in your environment or our hosted bench harness. Bench harness outputs CSV with p50/p95/throughput and cost delta.
[00:08:30] [00:08:40] Samira: I'm uploading the benchmark sheet link into the chat now: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/pioneer-demo-0304 (note: placeholder)
